clue.text: Motivated folk falter with stress getting out of hand

indicators.note: things getting out of hand go wild, so the two words falter and stress are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Keen go-getters wobble when pressure becomes too much to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out of hand' scrambles FALTER and STRESS together.
explanation.definitionFit: People who need no prompting from others to begin work are self-motivated, the classic description of these go-getters.

clue.text: One may want to know what's in store

definitions.text: One may want to know what's in store

parts.words: One may want to know what's in store
parts.note: the phrase 'what's in store' usually means what the future holds, but here it is literally the goods inside a shop

explanation.surface: Someone curious about what fate has planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's in store' reads as an idiom about the future; taken literally it is the stock in a shop, which a customer browsing wants to know about.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer browsing the shelves wants to see what stock the shop carries.

clue.text: Left port with cargo on board?

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship that sailed off from the harbour loaded with goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Aden is a seaport in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carrying a heavy load of goods is described as loaded or weighed down.

clue.text: Don't chuck everything — this may be useful for repair

definitions.text: Don't chuck everything — this may be useful for repair

parts.words: Don't chuck everything — this may be useful for repair
parts.note: keeping back a component rather than throwing it all away gives a spare piece for mending things later

explanation.surface: Advice from a hoarder: keep some bits back, they might fix something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'don't chuck everything' as 'spare a part', i.e. keep one piece back.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement component kept in reserve is used to mend a machine when an original one fails.

clue.text: Book of information unopened

indicators.note: a thing left unopened has lost its front, so the first letter of the word for information is dropped

parts.note: facts are pieces of information

explanation.surface: A volume of data whose cover nobody has lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the first letter, F, from FACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament, usually just called by this short name.

clue.text: Dismissed end to end, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word meaning from end to end is taken for its sound

parts.note: throughout means from one end to the other

explanation.surface: Someone sent packing, rumour has it, from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject an idea or eject a person is to get rid of them, the phrasal verb in past tense.

clue.text: Following game, lord briefly makes money

indicators.note: the lord piece comes after the game piece in the answer

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: said briefly, a word loses its last letter

parts.note: a peer is a lord

explanation.surface: After a sporting contest, a nobleman cashes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter from PEER, leaving PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of India and Pakistan, among others, is a unit of cash.

clue.text: A bar on flight

parts.note: it reads like a ban on air travel or a drinks counter on a plane, but the flight is a staircase and the bar a metal rod holding the carpet

explanation.surface: A drinks counter on an aeroplane, or a ban on flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The flight is a set of steps; the bar is a rod holding the carpet against each step.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal rod clamping carpet into the angle of each step on a staircase.

clue.text: Pair getting fever in foreign capital

parts.note: an ague is a shivering fever, like malaria

explanation.surface: A couple fall ill while abroad in a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of the Czech Republic, foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Picture someone nearing the end of his days in the staff room?

definitions.meaning: a painting by a great European artist of the period before about 1800

definitions.text: someone nearing the end of his days in the staff room?
definitions.meaning: an aged schoolteacher in the teachers' common room, close to retiring

explanation.surface: A painting of an ageing teacher close to retirement in the school staff room.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by a great pre-1800 European artist; jokingly, also an elderly male schoolteacher.

clue.text: Dad's half-hearted spiel

indicators.note: the heart of the word for spiel is its doubled middle letter; losing half of it removes one of them

parts.note: patter is glib talk, a sales spiel

explanation.surface: A father's sales pitch lacks enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' takes one of the two central Ts out of PATTER. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for father, used as an old-fashioned public-school word for one's dad.

clue.text: Better person steering a course on the river?

definitions.text: person steering a course on the river?
definitions.meaning: someone propelling a flat-bottomed boat with a pole

explanation.surface: An improved person navigating along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is read as one who bets, not as 'improved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler at the bookies, and someone poling a flat-bottomed boat along a river like the Cam.

clue.text: Act of cleaner gets son crying

parts.note: weeping means crying

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's behaviour leaves her boy in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing the floor with a broom is one of the main tasks of anyone who cleans.

clue.text: With drinks coming round, graduate dances

indicators.note: the word for drinks comes round the graduate, enclosing it

parts.note: rums are drinks
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate dances while the drinks are passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballroom dances of Cuban origin, in the plural like the clue word.

clue.text: Spy hugs English copper, having left bit of stuff

indicators.note: the spy word hugs, or wraps around, the following letters

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An agent embraces an English policeman before departing with some material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element here; 'bit of stuff' is the definition, not a pick of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a substance, a group of bonded atoms, is a tiny piece of matter.

clue.text: Like some purchases, no longer having to work?

definitions.meaning: goods bought at airports without tax
free from duty, i.e. let off your obligations

explanation.surface: Shopping as someone newly released from their obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport goods sold without import tax; whimsically, someone released from their obligations.

clue.text: Day out is fantastic, I admitted? Absolutely right!

indicators.note: the I is let in among the rearranged letters
fantastic suggests wild fancy, so the letters of day out is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that the trip was wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' scrambles DAYOUTIS and 'admitted' lets I in.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of strong agreement, telling a speaker they have put it exactly.

clue.text: Picture house and record memory

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
RAM is random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A cinema with recording equipment and a store of memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional image made with lasers is a kind of image.

clue.text: Member of family telling a story?

definitions.meaning: a relative, such as a cousin
the act of relating, or narrating, a tale

explanation.surface: A relative spinning a yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman or kinswoman; also the act of narrating a story, from 'relate'.

clue.text: Once more model engineers must go to shed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Army engineers have to head off to a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is a verb here: to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshape or remould something is to form it again, a verb like 'model'.

clue.text: Sweet start to the week reportedly

indicators.note: a thing reported is told aloud, so the day word counts for its sound

parts.note: Sunday is often counted as the first day of the week

explanation.surface: Talk of a pleasant beginning to the week.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream dessert topped with sauce and nuts is a type of pudding.

clue.text: Former lover modelled in birthday suit?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
posed means modelled, as for an artist

explanation.surface: An ex sat for a painter wearing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked leaves the body uncovered and open to view.

clue.text: One bird also protecting a very different kind of bird

definitions.text: a very different kind of bird

indicators.note: the two words around it shield the letter for one between them

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
too means also
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A cockerel and another bird guard a third, quite unlike them.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested parrot of Australasia is a bird nothing like a farmyard cockerel.

clue.text: Snake more angry concealing head

indicators.note: hiding the head of the word for more angry removes its first letter

parts.note: madder means angrier

explanation.surface: An enraged serpent hides its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing head' drops the M from MADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The common European viper, Britain's only venomous serpent.

clue.text: Character to declare a truce

definitions.meaning: to settle a quarrel and be friends again

explanation.surface: A figure who announces a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature or composition; as a two-word verb, to be reconciled after a quarrel.

clue.text: Choose to put up with the Left rather than the Right

indicators.text: with the Left rather than the Right
indicators.note: an L stands in where the R of the word for put up was

parts.note: to erect is to put up, as a building

explanation.surface: A voter decides to tolerate the Left instead of the Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like tolerate, but 'put up' is ERECT and the rest swaps its R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote someone into office is to pick them.

clue.text: Female and male needing help

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A woman and a man both requiring assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or young unmarried woman; old-fashioned, also a female servant.

clue.text: When suffering setback, boy gets healthy food

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backwards, so the word for when is reversed

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy who has had a setback gets a nutritious meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw vegetables and leaves is the classic wholesome meal.

clue.text: Once again attend to study and get into gear

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
to dress is to put on one's gear, or clothes

explanation.surface: Revisit some work, studying hard and getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into gear' is not about starting up but about putting clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a problem anew, to tackle or redress a matter a second time.

clue.text: Peer admitted being naughty is deliberate

indicators.note: letters being naughty misbehave and fall out of order, so peer admitted is rearranged

explanation.surface: A lord confessed that his misbehaviour was intentional.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned in advance and so intentional, the adjective sense of the clue word.
